content.description: Text of the reply; may be empty.

anyOf.description: Look up the customer's profile, plus any notes that human reviewers have left about them. The customer is the one this run is about, so no arguments are needed.
Look up a transaction's details: merchant, amount, country, time and so on.

transaction_id.description: The ID of the transaction, for example "TX-1003".

anyOf.description: Record your decision on a transaction. Call this exactly once for every transaction.

confidence.description: How sure you are of your score, from 0 (guessing) to 1 (certain).

decision.description: "approve" to let the payment through, or "block" to stop it.

reason.description: One or two sentences explaining your score.

risk_score.description: How likely the transaction is to be fraud, from 0 (certainly fine) to 100 (certainly fraud).

transaction_id.description: The ID of the transaction you assessed.

request.system:
# Transaction monitor

You are a fraud analyst monitoring card transactions for one bank customer.
Transactions arrive one at a time, as a transaction ID. For each new transaction:
1. Call get_transaction to look up its details.
2. Call get_customer_profile to see the customer's usual behaviour and any notes from human reviewers.
3. Compare the transaction with the profile and with the customer's earlier transactions in this conversation.
4. Call record_decision exactly once.
5. Reply with one short sentence summarising your decision.

Scoring guide:
- 0-30: normal for this customer.
- 30-70: unusual, but could easily be legitimate.
- 70-100: likely fraud, for example impossible travel between countries, or large purchases at high-risk merchants.

Set confidence below 0.7 when the evidence is mixed, for example travel the customer hasn't told us about.
Set it high when the case is clear either way.

response.content: Blocking TX-2004: a €1,800 in-person jewellery purchase in Singapore is far outside this Lisbon customer's usual categories and amounts, and there are no travel notes.

args.reason: €1,800 in-person jewellery purchase in Singapore. That is 4.5x the top of the usual €5-400 range, in a category the customer never uses, in a country other than home (PT), with no reviewer notes about travel.
